jobs.raw_description: Join Data Eminence as a remote AI/ML Engineer and contribute to designing, developing, and deploying intelligent applications powered by artificial intelligence and machine learning. You will work on data preprocessing, model development, predictive analytics, generative AI integrations, model evaluation, and AI-powered application features. The ideal candidate has a strong foundation in Python, machine learning, mathematics, and software development. This role provides hands-on experience with modern AI frameworks, large language models, data pipelines, model deployment, and intelligent application development. Full Description At Data Eminence , we use artificial intelligence and data-driven technologies to develop practical solutions for real-world challenges. As an AI/ML Engineer, you will collaborate with developers, analysts, and technical teams to build machine learning models and integrate intelligent functionality into applications. Your responsibilities will include: Collect, clean, preprocess, and analyze datasets. Develop and train machine learning models. Implement classification, regression, clustering, and prediction algorithms. Perform feature engineering and data transformation. Evaluate model performance using appropriate metrics. Experiment with model architectures and hyperparameter tuning. Work with deep learning frameworks for AI applications. Integrate AI models into backend services and APIs. Explore large language models and generative AI applications. Develop AI-powered workflows using external model APIs. Assist with prompt engineering and retrieval-augmented generation systems. Build reusable data-processing and machine learning pipelines. Monitor model performance and identify opportunities for improvement. Optimize inference performance and application reliability. Collaborate with software developers to integrate AI functionality. Maintain documentation for models, experiments, and workflows. Follow responsible AI practices, including data privacy and model evaluation. Research emerging AI technologies and development approaches. We believe in learning by doing. You will gain practical experience with Python, NumPy, Pandas, Scikit-learn, TensorFlow, PyTorch, SQL, Jupyter Notebook, LLM APIs, prompt engineering, embeddings, vector databases, RAG, REST APIs, Docker, cloud platforms, and AI development tools . This is a hands-on AI engineering role where you will develop intelligent features, experiment with machine learning models, integrate AI services, and gain practical experience building AI-powered applications. Requirements Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Artificial Intelligence, Data Science, Engineering, Mathematics, or a related field. 0–2 years of experience in AI, machine learning, data science, or relevant projects. Our mission is to make powerful AI accessible and useful for India, building technology that works across languages, industries and real-world use case...
jobs.raw_description: About Sarvam AI Sarvam AI is building India's sovereign AI stack, spanning foundational models, infrastructure and applications. Our mission is to make powerful AI accessible and useful for India, building technology that works across languages, industries and real-world use cases. As we continue to build and scale our products, understanding how people interact with them becomes increasingly important. We're looking for a curious and research-oriented intern to help us understand our users better and shape the experiences we build. The Role As a Product User Research Intern, you'll work closely with our product, design and engineering teams to understand user behaviour, identify friction points and uncover opportunities to improve our products. You'll interact directly with developers, product managers and founders, study how they use Sarvam's products, and translate your findings into actionable insights that influence product and design decisions. This is an opportunity to work on a new user research function at Sarvam, helping establish research practices and processes from the ground up. You'll also get ownership of a primary product area and the opportunity to see your research translate into real product improvements. What You'll Work On Understand our users: Conduct user interviews, surveys and usability studies with developers, PMs and founders to understand their needs, behaviours and challenges. Improve product experiences: Research user journeys across Sarvam's developer console, playground, API documentation and applications. Identify friction points across onboarding, API key creation, first API calls, billing and other key workflows. jobs.raw_description: About Us Resollect builds software that banks and asset reconstruction companies (ARCs, firms that take on loans that have stopped being repaid and work to recover them) use to manage loan recovery and the legal process around it. Recovering a loan can involve many parties, deadlines and court steps, and our tools help lenders keep all of it organised and moving. Role: Operations Associate Apply here: https://helios.resollect.com/apply/operations-associate The Role This is a broad operations role at Resollect, where you'll help keep the company running day to day while making the work itself faster and smarter. You'll be the person our clients and vendors deal with, you'll own operational tasks from start to finish, and you'll use AI to take the repetitive work off everyone's plate. One day you're on calls and follow-ups keeping a client and a vendor moving in step, the next you're building a small automation so a weekly report puts itself together, and the day after you're refining the prompts behind one of our internal AI tools. We're big on AI here. When something needs doing, we reach for AI first, build our own tools and automate the boring parts, and in this role that's your everyday way of working. What You'll Do • Front client and vendor relationships: You'll be the main point of contact for clients and vendors, handling the calls, follow-ups and coordination that keep everyone moving. • Own operations end to end: Whatever needs doing to keep things running, you'll take it from start to finish rather than passing pieces along. • Automate the repetitive work: When a task is dull and keeps coming back, you'll use AI to automate it instead of grinding through it by hand. • Build your own tools and workflows: You'll put together small tools and workflows that make you and the rest of the team faster. • Write and refine prompts: You'll do hands-on prompt engineering for our internal AI tools, testing and improving prompts until they reliably do their job. • Keep records and reports in order: You'll maintain records and pull together reports so that nothing slips through the cracks. • Fix what's broken or slow: You'll spot where things are stuck or slow, then fix them yourself or build something that does. What We're Looking For • High agency: You figure things out on your own and act without waiting to be told what to do next. • AI-native: You already use AI every day and build with it, so reaching for it first is how you work, not something you'd need to learn here. • Extremely organised: You track everything, close loops and follow up, which matters when clients and vendors are counting on you to keep things moving. • Scrappy and adaptable: You're comfortable when the path isn't fully mapped out, and you'll work with what you have to get something done. • Low ego, high curiosity: You're happy to take on whatever task needs doing, and you want to understand how every part of the business works. Nice to Have (Not Required) • Operations or client-facing experience: A previous internship or job in operations, coordination or client-facing work will help you settle in quickly. • A record of building things: Side projects, automations or tools you've made yourself are something we'd love to see. • Interest in fintech, legal-tech or AI: Curiosity about fintech, legal-tech or bringing AI into traditional industries will make this work even more interesting for you. Why This Might Be Worth Your Time • See every part of a startup: In a small, founder-led team, you'll touch every part of how the company runs rather than one narrow corner of it. • Direct access to the founders: You'll work closely with founders who have deep expertise in this field, so your ideas go straight to the people who can act on them. • Room to grow: There's clear room to take on more responsibility as you show what you can do. • AI as the default: You'll be encouraged to build your own tools and automate the boring work, which is a rare chance to make AI central to how you work from the start. Where and When Full-time, working from our office in Marol, Mumbai, six days a week. This role is aimed at people graduating in 2026 or 2027, and up to about two years of experience is welcome too. If you're the kind of person who figures things out without being asked, reaches for AI before doing anything by hand, and never lets a follow-up slip, we'd love to hear from you, so please apply.

jobs.raw_description: Company Overview Jetbro is a technology consulting and systems integration firm. We build reliable, scalable digital systems for organizations where technology is central to operations. Our clients range from Fortune 500 companies to high-growth startups across India, Australia and Canada. Our 50-member team works across custom product development, enterprise applications and infrastructure-led digital transformation. That spans systems integration, business process automation, cloud, data and applied AI, for industries including FMCG, supply chain, energy, healthcare and education. Our philosophy is simple: build systems that work quietly, predictably and under pressure. We value clarity over complexity and reliability over noise. Function over flash. Always. Every engagement starts with understanding how the business actually runs. Process Docs , our in-house method, takes a project from raw site notes to observations, process maps, PRDs, screen specs and a signed-off scope. That way the tech team builds exactly what the business needs. About the Role In this role, you turn how a business works into a precise blueprint a tech team can build from. We call this systems thinking: seeing a business as connected parts (people, operations, rules, data and handoffs) and designing how they should work together. The role sits close to a product manager, but starts earlier and goes deeper: on the operations floor. You will sit with operators, managers and finance teams, capture what really happens, and map it as a process. Then you will design the better version: the data it needs, the rules it must enforce, the screens people use, and what happens when something fails. Your output is the PRD, BRD and screen specs our engineers implement. You will do this work with AI as your main tool. Our Process Docs method runs inside Claude Code, and you will use it daily to capture, structure, review and refine documentation. This role suits someone early in their career who wants to learn how real businesses run and how good software is designed for them. Key Responsibilities Observe and capture. Visit client sites, shadow work and interview people. Record each activity's inputs, outputs, people, timing and problems, including the workarounds and exceptions nobody mentions at first. Map processes. Turn observations into step-by-step flows with every handoff, decision point and exception path named. A new employee should be able to follow your map on day one. Analyze and decide. Compare options, dig into the hard parts of a problem, and help settle the tech stack and implementation approach before design begins. Write PRDs and BRDs. Translate processes into requirements with IDs, business rules, data entities and acceptance criteria. Design the improved process, not a digital copy of the old one. Specify screens. For each screen, define entry points, layout, data shown, actions, validations, and empty, loading, error and restricted states. Design for correctness. Define the source of truth for each balance and status. Spell out how the system handles concurrent users, duplicate requests, partial fulfilment, cancellations and integration failures. Write the scope. Produce a self-contained scope document clients can read and sign off without opening anything else. Review and close gaps. Audit documentation for completeness, consistency and depth. Turn every gap into a specific question someone can answer. Stay with the build. Answer engineers' questions, review shipped work against acceptance criteria, and keep the PRD in step with what was built. Requirements Mandatory Requirements 0–2 years of work experience. Freshers with strong projects (in intern roles) are welcome. A degree in engineering, computer science or business, or equivalent proof of ability. We care more about how you think than what you studied. Strong critical thinking. You break a problem into parts, test assumptions, and spot what doesn't add up. You think beyond the obvious. You look past the process as described to the exceptions, workarounds and knock-on effects behind it. You ask sharp questions. In a room with a client, you ask the questions that reveal how the business really works: "Who decides that?", "Why is it done this way?", "What happens when this fails?" Strong communication, written and spoken. You can describe a process so someone who wasn't there understands it, and explain a design to a client and an engineer alike. Curiosity to learn, by nature. When something is outside your territory, you dive in with confidence and interest rather than waiting to be taught. Comfort reasoning about state and rules. Given "available = on-hand − held − reserved", you can trace balances through a sequence of actions without error. Basic software building ability. You can build and run a small application with persistent storage, using any stack you can defend. Hands-on use of AI coding tools, ideally Claude Code. You can direct an AI, check its output, and reject a wrong recommendation. Ability to read API contracts, sequence flows and acceptance criteria. Willingness to travel to client sites and spend time on factory floors, warehouses and offices. Good to Have Experience as an Associate Product Manager, or on a team building digital products. This is the strongest signal we look for. An internship in such a role counts. Exposure to operations domains: procurement, inventory, warehousing, sales order management, logistics or finance. An internship or project with a consulting, ERP or operations team. Familiarity with ERPs or low-code platforms such as SAP, Tally, Zoho, Odoo or Mendix, and how they integrate with custom systems. Understanding of transactions, idempotency, concurrency and audit trails in business software. Working knowledge of data modelling: entities, relationships, keys and constraints. You can sketch a schema for orders, stock and dispatches. Experience writing PRDs, user stories, wireframes or test cases. Comfort with Markdown, Git and diagram tools. Hindi, Gujarati or another regional language, for conversations on client sites. What we care about Reality over assumption. We document what actually happens, not what the SOP says. Workarounds and edge cases matter more than the happy path. Honest gaps. "I don't know yet" written down beats a confident guess. We mark unknowns and turn them into answerable questions. Specifics, not adjectives. "3–5 minutes per batch" beats "takes some time". Name the person, the system, the number. Failure is part of the design. A good spec says what happens when the network drops, the request repeats, or two people act at once. Accountability for AI output. AI makes us fast. You own every line it helps you produce, and you verify it. Builds, not decks. Our work is done when an engineer can build from it without guessing. About You You are at the start of your career and hungry to learn how businesses really work. You ask "how many?", "how often?" and "what happens when it breaks?" without being prompted. You enjoy untangling messy systems. You like both the conversation with a warehouse supervisor and the precision of a data model. You notice when two documents disagree on a number, and you fix it. You are curious by nature. A new industry, a new tool or an unfamiliar problem excites you more than it worries you, and you pick things up fast. You write clearly and briefly. You use AI tools well and are honest about what they got wrong. You would rather ship a spec that holds up under questioning than one that looks polished. Benefits Benefits This role is a strong first step toward a career in product management, consulting, tech sales or technology more broadly. Range of experience. You will talk to many clients across industries, and help design and build the systems they run on. Few early-career roles offer this breadth. Exposure to top-tier tech. You will work hands-on with modern AI tools, enterprise platforms and the engineering practices behind reliable systems. Real product work from the start. You will do the core work of a product manager: discovery, requirements, design, and seeing it through the build. Skills that travel. Understanding a business, asking the right questions and turning the answers into buildable systems are valued in product, consulting, sales and engineering alike. How we hire Our process has four stages. Each one decides whether you move to the next. Application review. We read your resume and your answers to a few short questions. HR round. A conversation about you, how you work, and whether Jetbro is the right fit. Assessment. A take-home exercise built around a real-world operations problem. You will design or build software for it using Claude Code, and submit a repository with your documentation and decisions. Technical round. You walk us through your assessment, defend your choices and answer questions on your experience and technical ability.

jobs.raw_description: This role will begin accepting applications on October 30, 2026, targeting cohort starts between April and August 2027 . You must complete your application *before* end of day on November 24, 2026 to be considered. Thank you in advance for your patience while our team reviews all applications. All applicants will be notified by the end of Spring 2027 with an update. In the “Resume" section, attach an updated CV or resume. No cover letter needed. In the “Higher education" section, fill out the fields accordingly and select “Now attending or Graduated” under "Degree status." Then, upload a current or recent unofficial or official transcript in English. Minimum qualifications: Currently enrolled in or graduated from a degree program within Product Management, Computer Science, Engineering, Data Science, Mathematics, Statistics, or a related technical field, or equivalent practical experience. Internship or Teaching Assistant experience in product management, software development or a similar technical field. Experience leading entrepreneurial efforts or outreach within organizations while building cross-functional relationships. Experience preparing and delivering technical presentations to an audience through internships, coursework, or extracurriculars. Preferred qualifications: Experience with methodologies aimed to drive product development and delivery. Experience applying Artificial Intelligence/Machine Learning (AI/ML) concepts to build products or features through relevant internship, capstone projects, or other academic work. Technical experience with programming languages, data analysis, business case/modeling, pricing, or design. Ability to start full-time in the primary cohort onboarding cycle between April and August 2027. Ability to communicate in English fluently to support cross-functional business relationships in the region. Excellent problem-solving, organizational, investigative, and critical thinking skills. About The Job At Google, we put our users first. The world is always changing, so we need Product Managers who are continuously adapting and excited to work on products that affect millions of people every day. In this role, you will work cross-functionally to guide products from conception to launch by connecting the technical and business worlds. You can break down complex problems into steps that drive product development. One of the many reasons Google consistently brings innovative, world-changing products to market is because of the collaborative work we do in Product Management. Our team works closely with creative engineers, designers, marketers, etc. to help design and develop technologies that improve access to the world's information. We're responsible for guiding products throughout the execution cycle, focusing specifically on analyzing, positioning, packaging, promoting, and tailoring our solutions to our users. Google aims to build products that organize the world's information and make it universally accessible to our users. As a Product Manager at Google, you could be working on new technologies, platforms, consumer facing products, and/or enterprise systems. The end goal will be to match you with the team that best aligns with your interests, experience, and where you will have the most impact. Responsibilities Understand markets and user requirements in depth. Launch products and features, test their performance, and iterate quickly. Work collaboratively with Engineering, Marketing, Legal, and User Experience (UX) on technologies. Develop innovative solutions to problems by collaborating as needed across regions, product areas, and functions. Google is proud to be an equal opportunity workplace and is an affirmative action employer. We are committed to equal employment opportunity regardless of race, color, ancestry, religion, sex, national origin, sexual orientation, age, citizenship, marital status, disability, gender identity or Veteran status. We also consider qualified applicants regardless of criminal histories, consistent with legal requirements. See also Google's EEO Policy and EEO is the Law. If you have a disability or special need that requires accommodation, please let us know by completing our Accommodations for Applicants form .
